text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The December quarterly Consumer Price Index figures, released yesterday, revealed that inflation had risen by 1.5 percent over the last year and that the underlying figure had continued to drop to 2.1 percent. Economists said this heralded a return to the low-inflationary environment of decades past. Page 1.

An Industry Commission report released yesterday states that, due to the previous Federal Government's legislation that allows mutual recognition of regulations professionals such as doctors and lawyers can now practice freely throughout Australia - increasing pressure on the professions to adopt national competency standards. Page 3.

Monsanto Inc has negotiated a research agreement with Charles Stuart University that will allow it to implement trails of weed resistance using manufactured chemicals to the popular herbicide Roundup. If confirmed, it will be the world's first instance of such resistance. Page 5.

In a case before the Industrial Relations Commission (AIRC), Victoria's Department of Education is seeking to prevent the State's teacher's union from having selection and promotion procedures included in awards covering Government schools. The case is being seen as a precedent in setting the limits of the AIRC's arbitration powers. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello unveiled a new Howard Government proposal yesterday which will see the Coalition try to capitalise on low inflation by claiming 1.3 million "battlers" are now assured of real wage rises under its planned A$8 "safety net" icrease in March. Page 1.

The New South Wales Industrial Relations Commission was told yesterday Channel 7 had subjugated well-known television personality Jana Wendt's professionalism and treated her as a "mere figurehead" on Witness when they stood her down on full pay from the current affairs program. Page 1.

Using research initially developed at the John Curtin School of Medical Research in Canberra, United States scientists have intensified the search for a cure for influenza by developing a pill that blocks an enzyme the influenza virus needs to replicate. Human trials of the anti-viral pill are set to begin in a few months. Page 1.

Australia's chief censor, John Dickie, told the country's most senior judges at the annual conference of Supreme Court and Federal Court judges in Brisbane yesterday the community was censoring itself, as shown by the hardening attitude towards violence on the screen, but he said society was becoming more tolerant towards on-screen sex and nudity if there was a reason for it. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Bureau of Statistics figures released yesterday show the inflation rate has hit its lowest level since the recession - it rose just 0.2 per cent in the December quarter, for an annual rate of 1.5 per cent, paving the way for another interest rate cut to combat persistently high unemployment. Page 1.

The latest round in the tussle between Jana Wendt and Channel Seven unfolded before a room of journalists and lawyers yesterday in the Industrial Relations Commission of New South Wales, where it was claimed Channel Seven had used Wendt's good standing to advance its own commercial interests at her expense. Page 1.

Speaking at the official opening of the South East Forests National Park, the 100th national park in New South Wales and the 38th opened in the State Government's 20 months, New South Wales Premier Bob Carr said the creation of such reserves is a very patriotic act as it is a gift to future generations. Page 1.

With Assistant Commissioner Christine Nixon at his side, Police Commissioner Peter Ryan this week summoned at least 12 of New South Wales' most senior police to the Hyde Park Plaza Hotel and told them they had been fired - the biggest single purge in the state's Police Service. Page 1.
THE AGE

After the release of figures yesterday which show that inflation levels are at 1.5 per cent - the lowest they have been in years, the Reserve Bank was called upon by business groups to cut interest rates. The Reserve Bank has cut interest rates from 7.5 to six percent since July. Page A1.

Among the ten people appointed to the Victorian Government's suicide prevention taskforce are the trucking magnate Lindsay Fox and the AFL player Jim Stynes. The taskforce, announced yesterday, will be headed by former senior public servant Peter Kirby, and was created after the State's suicide rate rose by 400 percent in the past decade. Page A1.

James Lewis, the six year old boy who yesterday became a hero after helping save his family from a car crash, has become a hot media property, with various current affairs shows offering thousands of dollars each for an interview. The boy's father however refused all offers saying that his son needed to return to normal life as soon as possible. Page A1&2.

Recently released internal documents have revealed that Melbourne's ambulance service did not put out to public tender A$1.5 million in consultancy work which was awarded to the company Intergraph, which runs the Metropolitan Ambulance Service's computer-ided dispatch service. Opposition health spokesman John Thwaites attacked the move as improper. Page A3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
